rationale: Revised the interface probe to close a limitation the account states: the missing StoreConfiguration callback was measured only after an AddVoter that moved an existing voter's address. The revision keeps that case and the ConfigurationStore-only control and adds two dual-interface cases triggered by different configuration commands, AddNonvoter for a new server and RemoveServer of a follower, so each case differs from the others only in the command that produces the LogConfiguration entry. Event names, measured fields and the recorder are unchanged; the trigger is now part of the case identity. Execution is requested, and the comparisons ask the documented callback to arrive in each case, which the earlier executions say it does not for the batched interface.

scope.description: Four cases, each a three-voter cluster built with the repository's own helper whose FSMs share a recorder: a ConfigurationStore-only FSM with a voter address change as the control, and three dual-interface FSMs whose single configuration change is a voter address change, an AddNonvoter, or a RemoveServer of a follower. Each case reports the StoreConfiguration and ApplyBatch configuration counts together with the command's result.
assumptions: All three commands are legal on a three-voter cluster: moving a voter's address keeps three voters, AddNonvoter adds a non-voter, and removing one follower leaves two voters, which is still a quorum.
Each case produces exactly one committed configuration entry, so the counts are comparable across cases.
As before, the recorder is shared across the cluster's FSMs so the counts answer whether the callback fires anywhere.
excluded: DemoteVoter and the deprecated Promote/AddStaging commands, and any multi-command sequence.

experiment.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with three peers, bootstrapping and the in-memory test configuration, and a MakeFSMFunc returning either an FSM implementing FSM and ConfigurationStore or one that also implements ApplyBatch, all recording into a shared recorder. The case emits assurance_config_store_setup with the batching flag, the trigger name, the leader and target identities and the peer count, then issues exactly one configuration command according to the trigger: AddVoter with a new address for the target voter, AddNonvoter for a fresh address-based identity, or RemoveServer of the target follower. It waits up to five seconds for either callback counter to become non-zero, waits a further 200ms, and emits assurance_config_store_result with the trigger, the batching flag, the command's error and the call counts. The harness is TestAssuranceConfigurationStoreWithBatching.

comparisons.description: Dual-interface FSM after an AddNonvoter: whether the documented callback arrives.
Dual-interface FSM after a RemoveServer: whether the documented callback arrives.
The standing case for the dual-interface FSM, re-measured alongside the new triggers.
Control: the ConfigurationStore-only FSM receives the callback, so any missing count is attributable to the batching interface rather than to the command.

experiment.revision_reason: The earlier revision triggered one configuration change only, by moving an existing voter's address, which the account records as a limitation. This revision adds two cases with the same dual-interface FSM but different commands, AddNonvoter and RemoveServer, and records the trigger in both events as part of the case identity. The control case and every measured field are unchanged.
